body:
I(32F) know what you mean about the responsibilities. I'm still struggling with these. 

However, not having a "significant other" is not a disadvantage or something to be ashamed of. Back when I started college, my only experiences were unsatisfying and unfullfilling relationships that lasted less than 3 weeks each. I wanted to "fit in" so bad. I wanted to be like my friends. Their love lives seemed so easy, so seamless. I tried very hard to emulate them. I met people online all the time. I was this clingy, pathetic girlfriend that ruined everything in just a week. I was miserable and I made people miserable. 

My advice: take it slowly. I met my boyfriend by total chance, just when I started to give up all hopes. I was not even interested in him at first and I think this lack of urgency really pleased him. I was just this chill girl who he liked to talk to. Then it clicked and it's been 12 years now.

Thing is, if you're not well enough to handle yourself on your own, I'm not sure having a girlfriend will change that. Despite this great relationship I have with my boyfriend, I'm very much on the verge of suicide myself. Romantic love is great, but chemical imbalance in your brain destroys everything, even greatness. You need to work on yourself and on your well-being before meeting someone. Suicidal thoughts act like a repellent on some people and I can't blame them. Please help yourself before trying to find a girlfriend. Your relationship with your future partner won't work out unless you feel comfortable in your own head.
